subject: Rate harmonization & packaging equalization — Exhibit pricing redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Porter <sarah.porter@novuscloud.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novuscloud.com, legal@novuscloud.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novus pricing exhibit — marked redlines and questions

Dylan / Marissa —

Attached is NovusCloud's mark-up of Exhibit C (pricing schedule) and the Order Form SKU matrix. Our counsel flagged a few areas that will require negotiation before procurement can get to an approval. High level concerns:

- Fee caps vs. per-SKU floors: the mark ups attempt to harmonize the caps across SKUs that are functionally the same across our multi-region deployments.
- Packaging equalization: we asked that equivalent feature bundles be billed consistently across Marketplace and direct order SKUs to avoid double-discounts.
- Transition proration: proposed a six-week proration for SKU swaps during migration windows.
- Cascade discounts: concerns that step-down discounts unintentionally cascade with volume true-ups.

We included comments in the PDF where we've suggested language and initial alternatives. Please confirm receipt and let me know who on your side can confirm whether consolidated caps across the Order Form are feasible from a billing and routing perspective.

Attachments: Novus_ExhibitC_pricing_marked.pdf (annotated), OrderForm_SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (SKU map)

Thanks,
Sarah Porter
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovusCloud

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Porter <sarah.porter@novuscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novus pricing exhibit — marked redlines and questions

Sarah — thanks, received and appreciate the clear annotations. I forwarded the marked Exhibit to our finance and product folks to validate the feasibility of harmonizing caps across those SKUs. Initial notes for you:

- We typically tie caps to the compute class (GPU tier) and expected token envelope. If the Novus SKUs you flagged map to the same compute class we can often align caps, but need to confirm billing SKU mapping in your matrix.
- Packaging equalization request makes sense from a customer fairness perspective; we just need to ensure Marketplace contractual constraints don't force different net rates.
- Six-week proration request is reasonable as a one-time migration concession; we'll need to route that through Billing to ensure it doesn't create automation exceptions.
- Cascade discounts: I agree we should clarify step-down language so true-ups don't double count multi-tier credits.

Marissa / Karthik — can you take a look at the attached Novus PDF and the SKU matrix and advise on two things: (1) operational feasibility to harmonize caps across the referenced SKUs and (2) acceptable language for a single-line proration clause that Billing can automate? I'm hoping to come back with a proposed compromise by EOD Monday.

Sarah — I'll set up a 30-min sync early next week to walk through any open line items; if you'd prefer a redline we can send a counter-markup instead.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Novus pricing exhibit — operational read + suggested language

Dylan / Karthik — quick operational read and proposed working language below (feel free to edit). I reviewed Novus's SKU matrix and the annotated Exhibit C. Summary and recommended positions: 

1) Harmonized caps across like-for-like SKUs
- Finding: The five SKUs Novus flags (NC-G1, NC-G1-MARKET, NC-G1-HYBRID, NC-G1-ISV, NC-G1-REG) map to the same GPU class (A100 equivalent) and identical token allowances in our catalog.
- Recommendation: We can accept a single fee cap across those SKUs with the following constraint: caps apply per billing account and are aggregated by "compute profile" as defined in Appendix A (we'll add a short definition).
- Suggested clause (for Exhibit C, Section 2.3): "Where multiple SKUs map to a single compute profile, the Fee Cap set forth in this Exhibit shall apply to the aggregate usage for that compute profile for the billing period, provided that Redwood may allocate usage across SKUs for invoicing purposes consistent with the Order Form SKU mapping."

2) Packaging equalization across Marketplace vs Direct SKUs
- Finding: Marketplace terms may prevent us from offering identical net rates on Marketplace-listed SKUs; however, we can offer feature parity and a crediting mechanism.
- Recommendation: Offer a "Market Parity Credit" that triggers when a Marketplace-billed SKU results in a higher gross rate — essentially a true-up credit on the next invoice. Limit: one true-up per SKU migration event, not an ongoing adjustment.
- Suggested clause: "If Marketplace billing results in a higher gross charge for equivalent features, Customer may request a Market Parity Credit; such credit shall be processed as a one-time invoice adjustment within the following billing cycle upon receipt of Customer's substantiating invoice and SKU mapping."

3) Migration proration (six weeks)
- Recommendation: Accept a 42-day proration window for SKU swaps during an agreed migration period, with automation guardrail: proration will be calculated pro rata by calendar day and capped at the difference between prior and new SKU gross rates.
- Suggested language: "For approved Migration Events, charges for replaced SKUs will be prorated for a period not to exceed 42 days from the effective date of the first SKU swap, calculated on a per-calendar-day basis and subject to the cap described herein."

4) Cascade discounts and true-ups
- Recommendation: Clarify that volume-tier discounts and ad-hoc promotional credits are applied in a defined order to prevent double-counting. Propose ordering: (a) SKU-level promotional credits, (b) volume-tier discounts, (c) Market Parity Credit, (d) invoice-level reconciliations.
- Suggested redline snippet: "Discounts and credits shall be applied in the following sequence ..." (we'll draft exact ordering for Exhibit language).

Next steps: If that approach aligns with you Dylan, I'll craft a single integrated redline (tracked PDF) with these clauses inserted and resend to Novus. Also need Legal to confirm whether the compute profile definition suffices or if they want explicit per-SKU enumerations.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none (working draft to follow).

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Porter <sarah.porter@novuscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com, procurement@novuscloud.com
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus pricing exhibit — rate harmonization proposal and next steps

Sarah — thanks for the redlines and for the patience while we operationalized the ask. We reviewed internally and can propose the following compromise for your team to review (I attached an integrated PDF):

- Harmonized caps: Redwood will apply a single Fee Cap across like-for-like SKUs mapped to a single compute profile (we've added a one-paragraph compute profile definition in Exhibit C).
- Market Parity Credit: we will provide a one-time Market Parity Credit for Marketplace-to-Direct parity issues, processed as a true-up on the next invoice after Novus provides the supporting invoice and SKU mapping.
- Migration proration: accepted up to 42 days (six weeks) for agreed migration windows; proration caps and automation guards included.
- Discount ordering: proposed sequence added to Exhibit C to avoid cascading true-ups; this will be the canonical application order for credits/discounts.

Open items: 
- Legal: need confirmation whether Novus needs explicit per-SKU enumerations instead of compute profile language (Marissa has noted we can list SKUs in Appendix if preferred).
- Procurement: please confirm whether Novus can accept the Market Parity Credit as a one-time adjustment and whether a maximum aggregate credit limit is required (we're prepared to cap total parity credits at 3% of the initial 12-month committed spend if you need guardrails).

If you're aligned, I'll circulate a tracked integrated redline (Exhibit C + Appendix A SKU map) for final review and then we can lock timing for signature. I can also set a 30-min call Monday to walk through any redline passages.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
